testDescription: From a single source IP, issue 11 POST /v2/auth/login requests within 60 seconds using valid credentials and required headers. Confirm the first 10 requests are not rate-limited and the 11th returns 429 with error: RATE_LIMITED and retry_after. After waiting for retry_after, verify login resumes normally.
prerequisites: Test user exists and is active with known credentials; Test harness can send HTTP requests from a single fixed IP; TLS 1.3 reachable at Base API URL; WAF/rate-limit policies enabled in the API Gateway.
stepsToPerform:
1) Prepare valid credentials for a test user: email='load.user@example.com', password='Str0ng!Passw0rd!'
2) Generate a valid anti-CSRF token value and note the single public IP the load generator will use
3) Start a 60-second window timer
4) Send Request #1: POST /v2/auth/login with JSON {email, password}, headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-CSRF-Token: '<token>' from the same IP; observe response
5) Repeat steps for Requests #2 through #10 within the same 60-second window, ensuring all are sent from the same IP and include X-CSRF-Token
6) For each of the first 10 responses, record status codes and verify none return 429
7) Send Request #11 within the same 60-second window from the same IP with the same headers and body
8) Observe Request #11 response and capture status, body fields, and headers
9) Assert Request #11 status is 429 and body contains error='RATE_LIMITED' and a numeric retry_after value
10) Wait the duration indicated by retry_after (in seconds)
11) Send Request #12 (same payload/headers) after the wait period
12) Verify Request #12 is not rate-limited (not 429) and returns a normal auth response (e.g., 200 with access_token or 401 for bad creds; rate-limit is cleared)
expectedResult:
- The first 10 login requests within a 60-second window from the same IP are not rate-limited (no 429 status)
- The 11th request within the same window returns HTTP 429 with body fields: error='RATE_LIMITED' and retry_after present
- After waiting retry_after seconds, a subsequent login request is accepted and not rate-limited

sourceCitation.excerpt: Rate limit exceeded (10 req/min per IP)

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: All login attempts (success or failure) count toward the per-IP rate limit; CSRF token format is accepted by gateway; Single-IP enforcement is active.

title: Verify Step 1 returns session_token for use in subsequent steps
description: Ensures Credit Application Step 1 returns a session_token and that it can be used immediately in Step 2 via X-App-Session. This protects step-chaining integrity. Automation: HIGH — pure API assertions.
testDescription: An authenticated user starts a new credit application with valid Step 1 personal information. The response should be 201 with application_id and session_token. The test then calls Step 2 with the session_token in header X-App-Session and receives 200 with PENDING_REVIEW and fico_pull_id, proving the token is usable in subsequent steps.
prerequisites: Active user account with verified email (e.g., 'applicant@example.com') exists; No active application in progress for this user; API reachable over TLS 1.3.
stepsToPerform:
1) Log in: POST /v2/auth/login with email='applicant@example.com', password='Str0ng!Passw0rd!', headers: Content-Type: application/json, X-CSRF-Token: '<token>'
2) Capture access_token from 200 response for Authorization: Bearer usage
3) Start application Step 1: POST /v2/applications/start with headers Authorization: Bearer <access_token>, X-CSRF-Token: '<token>', body including: full_legal_name='Alex Applicant', email='applicant@example.com', phone_number='+14165550123', residential_address {street='123 Test St', city='Toronto', province='ON', postal_code='M4B 1B3'}, id_type='PASSPORT', id_number='X9Z81AB123'
4) Observe response and verify HTTP 201
5) Extract application_id and session_token from the Step 1 response and persist for next call
6) Invoke Step 2: POST /v2/applications/{application_id}/financials with headers Authorization: Bearer <access_token>, X-CSRF-Token: '<token>', X-App-Session: <session_token>; body: employment_status='EMPLOYED', employer_name='TestCorp', gross_annual_income=85000.00, other_income omitted, monthly_rent=1500.00, existing_debt_payments=300.00, sin_consent=true
7) Observe Step 2 response and verify HTTP 200
8) Confirm Step 2 response includes status='PENDING_REVIEW' and a non-empty fico_pull_id
9) (Negative chaining check) Call Step 2 again without X-App-Session header (same payload) and observe response
10) Verify the missing session header call is rejected with HTTP 401 and error='SESSION_EXPIRED'
11) Cleanup note: No resource deletion required; application remains in progress per product workflow
expectedResult:
- Step 1 returns HTTP 201 with application_id and session_token fields present
- Step 2 called with X-App-Session=<session_token> returns HTTP 200 with status='PENDING_REVIEW' and fico_pull_id
- Step 2 call made without X-App-Session is rejected with HTTP 401 and error='SESSION_EXPIRED'

sourceCitation.location: Section 4 Credit Application Web Flow, Lines 111-115, 141-145
sourceCitation.excerpt: the system issues a session_token on Step 1 that must accompany Steps 2 and 3.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: Authorization header with Bearer token is required for application endpoints per system design; CSRF token required on POSTs.

title: Verify auto-scaling maintains throughput at 5,000 RPS when CPU hits 70%
description: Confirms the platform sustains 5,000 requests/second and triggers auto-scaling at 70% CPU utilization to preserve throughput. Automation: MEDIUM — requires load generation and infra metrics access.
testDescription: Generate a controlled load ramp to 5,000 RPS against a lightweight authenticated GET endpoint (account summary) from multiple clients. Monitor API gateway CPU and scaling events. Verify that at 70% CPU utilization, auto-scaling triggers and the system continues sustaining 5,000 RPS without throughput drop.
prerequisites: Performance test environment mirrors production scaling policies; Test account exists (account_id known) and owned by the test user; Load generator capable of sustained 5,000 RPS; Access to infra metrics and scaling event logs.
stepsToPerform:
1) Authenticate: POST /v2/auth/login to obtain access_token for a test user; store token for Authorization: Bearer
2) Validate target endpoint works: GET /v2/accounts/{account_id}/summary with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>; expect HTTP 200
3) Configure load plan: 1-minute warm-up at 1,000 RPS, then ramp linearly to 5,000 RPS over 2 minutes, then sustain 5,000 RPS for 5 minutes
4) Start warm-up and verify baseline responses are HTTP 200
5) Begin ramp-up to 5,000 RPS; continuously record responses/throughput and gateway CPU utilization
6) Upon reaching 5,000 RPS sustain phase, continue for 5 minutes while monitoring CPU; note the timestamp when CPU reaches or exceeds 70%
7) Observe auto-scaling signals (e.g., new gateway instances/pods) at or immediately after the 70% CPU threshold
8) During and after scaling, verify the system continues to deliver 5,000 RPS (no sustained dip in achieved RPS below target)
9) Spot-check a sample of responses (e.g., 1,000 random responses) for HTTP 200 status to confirm endpoint correctness under load
10) Continue monitoring for 2 additional minutes post-scale to ensure throughput stability
11) Stop the load; capture throughput, CPU, and scaling event timelines for evidence
expectedResult:
- Auto-scaling is triggered when the API gateway CPU reaches ~70% utilization (scaling event observed)
- Throughout the test, achieved throughput remains at or above 5,000 RPS during the sustain phase, without sustained drop during or after scaling
- Target endpoint continues responding with HTTP 200 under load

sourceCitation.excerpt: API gateway must sustain 5,000 concurrent requests/sec. Auto-scaling triggers at 70% CPU utilisation.

assumptions: ASSUMPTION: Observability provides CPU metrics and scaling event logs for the API gateway; The chosen GET endpoint is representative and not subject to per-IP rate limits under test configuration.
